quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the proper footwear for riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Shoes with long, loose laces.
Shoes with short heels.
Shoes with tall heels.
Always sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes with short heels.
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on surfaces. Tuck in laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: How much stopping distance do motorcycles need in traffic compared to cars?

options.text: Much less distance.
Less distance.
The same distance.
More distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same distance.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the same stopping distance as cars in traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Press the front brake hard to prevent the front tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes to slow down on slippery surfaces. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Other motorists have trouble seeing motorcycles at night. What should a motorcycle rider do?

options.text: Reduce speed when riding at night.
Use the horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Do not ride at night.
Stay directly in front of other vehicles so their headlights light you up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed when riding at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night: reduce your speed, increase your following distance, use other vehicles' headlights to see ahead, use your high beam headlight (unless following or meeting another vehicle), and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially helpful when riding through areas with potential hazards.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when the front brake is used.
Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes when either is used.
Remembers the rider's typical braking force.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when the rear brake is used.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What collects in the center portion of a traffic lane?

options.text: Debris and oil from cars.
This is where motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Most accidents happen here.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist here.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil from cars.
questions.explanation: Debris and oil from cars collect in the center of the lane. Utility hole covers and other hazards are also commonly found there.

questions.question: What braking mistake do most riders involved in crashes make?

options.text: They brake the front tire too little and the rear tire too much.
They brake the front tire too much and the rear tire too little.
They only use the front brake.
They only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: They brake the front tire too little and the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders involved in crashes brake the front tire too little and the rear tire too much.

questions.question: What percentage of motorcycle riders killed in crashes had been drinking?

options.text: 20 percent
40 percent
60 percent
80 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a major cause of motorcycle crashes and deaths. Studies show that about 40 percent of all riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Dress warmly.
Limit how far you ride each day.
Take frequent rest breaks.
Take artificial stimulants.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take artificial stimulants.
questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue, wear clothes that protect you from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants. When they wear off, you may feel extremely tired.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal stopping power.
The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
Use only the front brake when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides more stopping power than the rear brake—at least 70 percent of your total stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes provide all of the following, except:

options.text: Comfort.
Protection in a crash.
Protection from cold weather.
Discomfort.

questions.correctAnswerText: Discomfort.
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash. They also protect you from weather hazards like extreme heat or cold.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should you avoid?

options.text: The left part of the lane
The center part of the lane
The right part of the lane
No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position that is always best and none that should always be avoided. Choose a lane position that works for your current riding conditions.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the leader.
Close to the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should position themselves just behind the leader. This way, they will not fall behind the group. Experienced riders behind them can also watch and help them.

questions.question: When riding in a lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position that is always best or always wrong. Change your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: What vest or jacket color helps you be seen the most?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be seen better. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green are best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: How should you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Turn the handlebars quickly.
Shift your weight quickly.
Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane.
Change your lane position as conditions change.
Always ride in the center of the lane so others can see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as conditions change.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position that is always best or should always be avoided. Change your position based on changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left
The center
The right
It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may tempt the driver to cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle or one with a sidecar, why should you not ride too far to the right of your lane?

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side of a motorcycle. If you ride too far right, the sidecar can run off the road. The same is true for the rear right wheel of a three-wheeled motorcycle if you get too close to the road edge.

questions.question: What should a rider do in a slow, tight turn?

options.text: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
Lean at the same angle as the motorcycle.
Lean in the opposite direction of the motorcycle and the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright while your body leans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your body upright while the motorcycle leans.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, lean at the same angle as your motorcycle. In slow, tight turns, keep your body upright to counterbalance the leaning motorcycle.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane give a motorcyclist?

options.text: One
Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths: left, center, and right. Motorcyclists can use any of these positions.

questions.question: What should you do if rain starts while you are riding?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Increase your speed.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that make it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars where it is safer. Also slow down on wet surfaces.

questions.question: How often should you check a motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular pre-ride checks help keep your motorcycle safe.
